evals.name: settings-airplane-mode-script
evals.prompt: Write me a shell script that uses the baguette CLI to: (a) find a booted iPhone simulator, (b) press Home, (c) tap the Settings app icon on the home screen, (d) wait for Settings to open, (e) capture a single JPEG frame proving Settings is on screen, and save it to /tmp/settings.jpg. Assume baguette is installed and at least one iPhone is booted. Be concrete with the actual commands and the wire-format JSON the script needs. Inline any tap coordinates with comments explaining how you derived them.
evals.expected_output: A bash script that uses `baguette list --json` to pick a UDID, `baguette describe-ui` to get the screen size in points (its outer `screen`), `baguette press --button home`, `baguette tap` with width/height passed in (NOT normalized 0-1 coords), and `baguette screenshot --output /tmp/settings.jpg` for the proof. Better still if it finds the Settings icon with `baguette describe-ui` and taps its frame's centre. Should NOT cut frames out of `baguette stream`, and should NOT propose `baguette key` or `baguette type`.

evals.name: maps-pinch-stream
evals.prompt: I need to stream a series of gestures to a long-running baguette session: open Maps, then perform a smooth two-finger pinch-to-zoom-in on the centre of the screen, then pan north by 200 points. The simulator is an iPhone 17 Pro Max (UDID: AAAA-BBBB-CCCC-DDDD). Generate the exact newline-delimited JSON I should pipe into `baguette input --udid AAAA-BBBB-CCCC-DDDD`, including any home/launch steps. Explain why you're using `touch2-*` vs `touch1-*` for the pinch.
evals.expected_output: Newline-delimited JSON using `touch2-down/move/up` (NOT touch1) for the pinch, with x1/y1/x2/y2 in device points, width/height on every gesture taken from `describe-ui`'s outer `screen` (438x954 is the doc's iPhone 17 Pro Max example; a live read wins). Should explain that single-finger streaming routes correctly but iOS treats it as a pan, not a pinch — so two-finger is required for UIPinchGestureRecognizer.

evals.name: type-text-fallback
evals.prompt: Write a baguette command that types the text 'hello' into a TextField that's currently focused on the booted iPhone simulator. The UDID is XXXX-YYYY.
evals.expected_output: `baguette type --udid XXXX-YYYY --text hello` (US-ASCII keystrokes into the focused field). Mentions that non-ASCII text would need `baguette paste` instead. Should NOT fall back to `xcrun simctl io` or AXe.

evals.name: set-simulated-location
evals.prompt: Using the baguette CLI, set the booted iPhone simulator's location to the Eiffel Tower (48.8584, 2.2945), then simulate driving from San Francisco (37.629538, -122.395733) to New York City (40.628083, -73.768254) at 260 m/s. The UDID is ZZZZ-WWWW. Give me the exact commands.
evals.expected_output: Uses `baguette location set --udid ZZZZ-WWWW 48.8584,2.2945` (a single lat,lon TOKEN, not --lat/--lon flags) and `baguette location start --udid ZZZZ-WWWW --speed 260 37.629538,-122.395733 40.628083,-73.768254` (two-plus lat,lon tokens). Should NOT invent a SimulatorHID/gesture path — this is a `simctl location` path. Bonus: notes that a token whose latitude starts with `-` needs a `--` separator, and that `baguette location clear` restores live location.

evals.name: seed-onboarding-defaults
evals.prompt: Before my UI test runs I want the app com.example.notes to think onboarding is already done. Its SwiftUI code reads @AppStorage("onboarded") as a Bool. The app is already running on the booted simulator (UDID 1111-2222). What baguette commands do I run, and will the running app see the change?
evals.expected_output: Uses `baguette defaults write --udid 1111-2222 --bundle-id com.example.notes --key onboarded --type bool --value true`, and addresses the running app: `--relaunch-if-needed` (an @AppStorage key changes live) or `--relaunch`. May mention `defaults read` to verify. Should NOT edit plist files by hand or use `xcrun simctl spawn defaults`.

evals.name: tap-button-by-label
evals.prompt: On the booted simulator (UDID 3333-4444) my app shows a button labelled "Sign In" but I don't know where it is on screen. Use baguette to tap it.
evals.expected_output: Runs `baguette describe-ui --udid 3333-4444`, finds the node whose label is "Sign In", and taps the centre of its frame (x + width/2, y + height/2) with `baguette tap`, passing `describe-ui`'s outer `screen` width/height (device points, same units as the frame). Should NOT guess coordinates from a screenshot alone.

evals.name: paste-unicode
evals.prompt: Type the string "Café — 東京 🍣" into the focused search field on simulator 5555-6666 with baguette.
evals.expected_output: Uses `baguette paste --udid 5555-6666 --text "Café — 東京 🍣"` because `type` / `key` are US-ASCII only. Should NOT use `baguette type` for this string.

evals.name: offline-test-relaunch
evals.prompt: My app com.example.feed should show an offline banner. Using baguette on simulator 7777-8888, put the device offline, check the banner appears, then restore the network.
evals.expected_output: `baguette network set --udid 7777-8888 --offline`, then relaunches the app (`xcrun simctl launch --terminate-running-process 7777-8888 com.example.feed`) because only apps launched after arming are conditioned, verifies with `baguette screenshot` or `describe-ui`, and finishes with `baguette network clear`. Notes that WKWebView content and SDKs with their own sockets are not conditioned.

evals.name: duo-unfolded-tap
evals.prompt: On an iPhone Duo simulator (UDID 9999-0000), unfold it and tap the centre of the unfolded screen with baguette.
evals.expected_output: `baguette hinge --udid 9999-0000 --pose open`, then reads the new size from `baguette describe-ui`'s `screen` (the unfolded panel, not the cover), then `baguette tap` at half of that width/height with those width/height values. Should NOT reuse the folded cover's size or look for a `--display inner` flag.
